premise: A plotter exploration forked from the daily archive piece 'Overstruck' (Day 147). The daily track asks what a Noah source reduces to in the engine's own vocabulary; this strand asks what the line-printer piece becomes when a PEN — not a screen — makes its marks. The parent's canonical raster is never altered. Everything here is either a faithful translation of that parent to pen (a rendition) or a study that deliberately leaves it behind.

forkRule.line: Fidelity. A plot is a faithful EXPORT while it still reproduces the parent's checksum; it becomes a STUDY the moment a decision changes what is DRAWN, not just how it is output.
forkTriggers: a different glyph vocabulary, or a re-seeded / re-composed layout
tone remapped to exploit ink/pen behaviour (would no longer match the raster)
multi-pen / colour separation — more than one pen layer with intent
an engine capability built for pen aesthetics rather than to reduce a Noah source
a series: a 2nd/3rd variation kept as an artwork in its own right
forkRule.tell: When the pen stops reproducing the piece and starts making decisions the screen never made.

parent.title: Overstruck
parent.note: Canonical seed lives in selected-genomes.json (day 147) and is NEVER changed by this track. Full genome is the single source of truth there.

setup.pen: Sakura Pigma Micron 05 — archival pigment ink (~0.45 mm nib)
setup.exporter: exportPlotterSVG — stroke-only, single pen, real mm units, bed-fit + ink-centred, single-stroke plotter-font caption (v3.18.1–.6, all export-only, raster untouched)
setup.calibration: Solid-fill swatch plotted 2026-10-25 on light-gray stock: 0.40 solid, 0.45 solid (widest that still reads solid), 0.50 visibly lined. Pitch = nib width (0.45) gives edge-to-edge solid; 0.50 > nib opens gaps. Picked 0.45 mm (0.40 is the denser fallback).
setup.pens_on_hand: black Sakura Micron 05 (~0.45mm) + a very thin red (fine nib) — weight contrast is intentional

renditions.caption: pen strokes, discreet footer (title 3.2 / meta 2.3 mm) so the art dominates — title · date·makers · via @Noahbolanowski · Mechanical Reverie
renditions.note: PRIMARY plot-ready sheet. Calibrated to the pen (0.45 mm) and with a small signature so it sits as a quiet footer rather than competing with the fine line-printer marks.
renditions.plotted: 2026-10-25 — AxiDraw V3/A3, Micron 05, hatch 0.45mm. First physical realization of a Mechanical Reverie piece.
renditions.plotFinding: On paper the glyph ramp reads as TEXTURE, not tone: # → crosshatch, ▓/█ → horizontal stripes, so the former solid-black cores read as another pattern rather than black fill (crosshatch # even competes with the hatch blocks for weight). The digital tonal depth becomes textural variety — faithful to Hammersley, but true solid black on paper would need a pen-first fill (a fork).

renditions.note: Solid-fill pitch calibration strip (0.40 / 0.45 / 0.50 / 0.55 / 0.60 mm) for the 0.5 mm pen. Pick the widest pitch that still reads solid on paper, then re-export the parent at that pitch.

studies.title: Overstruck — Two Colour (Nested Regions)
studies.fork: Multi-pen colour separation — the raster has no colour-layer equivalent, so this leaves the parent behind (a true study, not an export).
studies.idea: Split the marks onto TWO pens by nested-rectangle ring: concentric regions of the lineprinter tone field alternate black / red, so the piece's stacked-rectangle structure becomes chromatic and the overprint reads where the two colours meet.
studies.note: 2 Inkscape layers (pen1 black, pen2 red) + black caption. Plot pen1, swap to red, plot pen2. Parent seed untouched.
studies.plotted: 2026-10-25 — AxiDraw, black Micron 05 + a VERY THIN red pen. First two-colour plot of the track.
studies.plotFinding: The thin red lays a lighter/finer line than the black, so the two pens differ in WEIGHT as well as hue: red nested zones RECEDE (a faint underlayer), black columns/#-blocks/solid ADVANCE. The concentric nested structure gains real depth (foreground/background), reading almost atmospheric — far richer than an equal-weight 2-colour plot. Pen-WEIGHT difference is now a deliberate lever for the track (pair a bold dark pen with a fine light one).

studies.title: Overstruck — Tonal Depth (Solid Black)
studies.fork: A pen-first fill that changes what is drawn: the dark glyphs fill the full cell so adjacent darks MERGE into true solid black on paper — restoring the digital tonal range the per-cell hatch lost. Direct answer to the first-plot finding.
studies.idea: Keep -, |, # as line-printer character texture, but render ▓/█ as full-cell fills at the pen pitch so they read as true solid black — the darkest cores become unambiguously the darkest, restoring light→dark depth in ink.
studies.note: Single black pen. Addresses the 2026-10-25 plot finding (texture-vs-tone): solids now merge to true black.
studies.plotted: 2026-10-25 — AxiDraw, Micron 05, 0.45mm. SUCCESS: the dark cores now read as filled dark blocks, clearly the heaviest marks; # sits back as medium crosshatch; tonal depth restored vs the first plot.
studies.plotFinding: Solids read as deep CHARCOAL-black, not dead-flat ink — fine horizontal striping is still visible in the smaller cores (Micron lays a hair under 0.45mm, so 0.45 pitch leaves micro-gaps; a large swatch integrates to solid, small cores less so). Hierarchy holds. For JET black: drop the solid-fill pitch (~0.35–0.40mm) or cross-hatch both directions — a one-line tweak (fullHatch).

openDirections: Tonal-depth study: a pen-first solid-fill (larger cells or scribble-fill) so █ reads as true black, restoring the digital tonal range on paper (a fork, not an export).
Multi-pen colour separation — the first likely true fork (the raster has no colour-layer equivalent).
A plotter-native glyph vocabulary (beyond the lineprinter ink-density set).
Re-seeded layout variations plotted as a series.
Overprint / layered passes exploiting ink build-up.

findings.finding: Pen translates the lineprinter ink-density ramp (space‹-‹I‹#‹▓‹█) into a TEXTURE vocabulary, not a tonal one. Darkness order is not preserved — crosshatch # reads as heavy as the solid-hatch █. Dash grounds and # grids are the strongest marks; the Micron holds a clean consistent line at 0.45mm.
findings.implication: A faithful plot = textural reading (good, Hammersley-true). For genuine tonal DEPTH / true black on paper, redesign the stroke-glyph fill for pen (bigger cells so hatch builds, or a blackout scribble-fill) — that CHANGES what is drawn, so it would be Study 01, not an export.
